'''Anne Patricia, Lady Thorne''' (born 3 October 1928) is a physicist specialising in [[atomic physics]] and [[spectroscopy]]. She is senior research fellow in physics and senior research investigator in the Department of Physics at [[Imperial College London|Imperial College of Science Technology and Medicine]]. She was the senior tutor for women students at Imperial College, and played a leading role in starting the Imperial College Day Nursery.

== Early life and education ==
Born Anne Patricia Pery, she attended [[Chelsea College of Arts|Chelsea Polytechnic]], where she sat the London University Intermediate examination in Physics, Chemistry, Pure and Applied Mathematics in 1946. This qualification enabled her to join Oxford University in 1947, where she was a member of [[St Hugh's College, Oxford]]. She received a BA Hons degree in Physics and Mathematics in 1950 and stayed on for a further four years as a post-graduate.<ref name=":0">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=OPutDgAAQBAJ&q=lady+anne+thorne&pg=PA203|title=Women At Imperial College; Past, Present And Future|last=Anne|first=Barrett|date=2017-02-24|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=9781786342645}}</ref>

== Career ==
After graduating and receiving her PhD, Thorne undertook a year-long research fellowship at [[Harvard University]], where she worked with [[Norman Foster Ramsey Jr.|Professor Norman Ramsey]].<ref name=":0" />

In 1955, Thorne joined Imperial College as an assistant lecturer in the Physics department.<ref name=":1">{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=bdC6CgAAQBAJ&q=lady+%22anne+thorne%22%2C+physicist&pg=PA334|title=History Of Imperial College London, 1907-2007, The: Higher Education And Research In Science, Technology And Medicine|last=Hannah|first=Gay|date=2007-02-14|publisher=World Scientific|isbn=9781908979445}}</ref> She was promoted to lecturer in Physics in 1956 and again in 1968 to senior lecturer.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://issuu.com/sthughscollegeoxford/docs/chronicle_1968-1969/35|title=St Hugh's College, Oxford - Chronicle 1968-1969|website=Issuu|date=6 October 2015 |access-date=2019-03-05}}</ref> During her time at Imperial College, she was the first person to take up the role of senior tutor for women students and successfully argued for the implementation of the Day Nursery, which opened in 1970.<ref name=":1" />

In the 1970s, Thorne worked on vacuum-ultraviolet [[interferometry]] and oscillator strengths by [[Mach–Zehnder interferometer|Mach–Zehnder interferometry]], and in 1974, she published the academic text book ''Spectrophysics'', which was subsequently rewritten as ''Spectrophysics: Principles and Applications'' in 1999.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RIcFAAAAIAAJ&q=%22anne+thorne%22+physicist+-architects|title=Scientific Research in British Universities and Colleges|date=1975|publisher=H.M. Stationery Office}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=SF8fdwacahkC&q=Spectrophysics%3A+Principles+and+Applications&pg=PA1|title=Spectrophysics: Principles and Applications|last1=Thorne|first1=Anne|last2=Litzén|first2=Ulf|last3=Johansson|first3=Sveneric|date=1999-04-01|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9783540651178}}</ref>

During her tenure at Imperial, Thorne's main non-scientific voluntary work was to improve education. She served on the Governing Boards of 8 different schools and Colleges, both State and Independent. She was the Chairman of Governors of [[Ardingly College]] for 5 years.<ref name=":0" />

== Retirement and legacy ==
Thorne retired in 1993, becoming senior research fellow in physics, and then senior research investigator in physics.

Imperial College awards a prize named for Anne Thorne each year to a student whose PhD thesis in experimental physics is concerned with the development or use of new experimental instruments or techniques.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.imperial.ac.uk/news/176744/cdt-student-wins-anne-thorne-thesis/|title=CDT Student wins Anne Thorne thesis prize|last=Dhulipapa|first=Veena|date=20 December 2016|website=Imperial News|access-date=2019-03-05}}</ref>

Thorne's former students endearingly termed her 'Lady squared'.<ref name=":0" />

== Family ==
Anne was the daughter of [[Edmund Pery, 5th Earl of Limerick|Edmund Colquhoun Pery, 5th Earl of Limerick]], and [[Angela Pery|Angela Olivia Trotter]].

In 1959 she married Lieutenant Colonel Sir [[Peter Francis Thorne]], with whom she had a son and three daughters.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.telegraph.co.uk/news/obituaries/1462804/Sir-Peter-Thorne.html|title=Sir Peter Thorne|date=2004-05-25|work=The Telegraph|access-date=2019-03-05|issn=0307-1235}}</ref>
